sponsors.name: Wayne State University
sponsors.desc: The Wayne State University College of Engineering sits at the center of Detroit, a few blocks from the industry that made the city — and it trains engineers accordingly. Its programs span biomedical, chemical, civil and environmental, computer science, electrical and computer, industrial and systems, and mechanical engineering, with graduate and research work tied closely to the mobility, manufacturing, and health-care employers in the region. The college draws one of the more diverse engineering student bodies in Michigan, many of them first-generation and commuting from the neighborhoods around campus, and it leans into that: co-ops and industry partnerships are the norm rather than the exception, and students tend to have real project work behind them before they graduate. Its home, the Anderson Engineering Building, gives the college modern teaching labs and collaborative space in the heart of the WSU campus — and makes it a fitting host for a summit about who gets to build what comes next.

community.name: SHPE Detroit
community.desc: SHPE Detroit is transforming lives in Detroit by inspiring and motivating young Hispanic students to excel in STEM education through mentorship and community involvement and enhancing career opportunities for Hispanics by building a strong professional network.

community.name: Compass Detroit
community.desc: The Collective of Minority Professionals and STEAM Societies (formerly COMPES) was formed in 2000 as an initiative between the NSBE, SHPE, and SWE Detroit professional chapters. The mission of this collaborative partnership is to support the local Detroit community in upskilling, career growth, networking, and to provide access to new opportunities.

community.name: NSBE Detroit
community.desc: Representing Black Engineers in Detroit. NSBE Detroit Professionals strive to increase technical awareness, encourage scholastic achievement, and stimulate enthusiasm in the black engineering community of Detroit. NSBE’s mission is to increase the number of culturally responsible Black engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally and positively impact the community. The NSBE Professionals inspire the next generation of technical professionals, and serve as a catalyst for transformation.

community.name: GM Cares
community.desc: GM Cares is General Motors' employee-driven volunteerism and global giving program that empowers workers to support local community causes. STEAM Education: Supporting multidisciplinary skill development and student tutoring. Road Safety: Improving vehicle access and safe driving habits. Community Impact: Organizing grassroots service projects, matching employee donations, and participating in initiatives like local food bank volunteering and disaster relief.

community.name: GM Latino Network
community.desc: The GM Latino Network is an employee resource group (ERG) at General Motors designed to connect Latino employees and promote awareness of Latino culture. Mission: Provide professional networking opportunities, support career growth, and spread cultural awareness within the company. Activities: Host community and educational events, such as STEM networking workshops for local students, and engage in community outreach.

community.name: Techqueria Detroit
community.desc: We’re a vibrant, 25,000-strong community empowering Latiné professionals to thrive in every corner of the tech industry. Techqueria provides mentorship, career development, and advocacy for DEI.
